origin: cwe/89 Key Principles: never allow untrusted input to directly control query construction; always parameterize

finding.name: SQL Injection
finding.sink_code: cursor.execute("SELECT id, name FROM customers WHERE name = '" + term + "'")
finding.summary: search_customers concatenates term directly into the SQL text. The browser-side submitSearch() escapes single quotes before sending the request, but that only affects requests made through the app's own JavaScript - any HTTP client (curl, a proxy, a script) can POST an unescaped term directly to the endpoint, so the server-side concatenation is exploitable regardless of what the client does.

trap: Treating the client-side escaping in search.js as evidence the finding is already mitigated, or adding a matching server-side .replace("'", "\\'") to match it, both miss the point: escaping is bypassable no matter where it runs client-side, since a request never has to go through search.js at all, and a hand-rolled escape (quote-doubling or backslash-escaping) is itself an incomplete defense against a database's actual quoting rules. The fix is parameterization at the server: cursor.execute("SELECT id, name FROM customers WHERE name = ?", (term,)), which the SQLite driver treats as a placeholder no matter what term contains - the client-side code becomes irrelevant to whether the query is safe.
must_preserve: search_customers still returns customers whose name exactly matches term for any legitimate search value. The client-side escaping in search.js is unrelated to this fix and does not need to change.
